headline: Regional Forest and River Recreation Access
reservation: Most public trails and river access points near Missoula do not require entry permits, but specific glamping and campsite locations require advance booking through private providers or the Forest Service. Demand for riverside lodging is high from June through September; check the official Recreation.gov site for changing seasonal windows and local fire restrictions.

days.title: Mountain Vistas and River Trails

stops.name: Mount Sentinel 'M' Trail
stops.detail: Climb the steep switchbacks to the iconic landmark for a panoramic view of the Clark Fork River and the Missoula valley.

stops.name: Riverfront Trail
stops.detail: Walk the paved path through the heart of the city to observe the local fly-fishing culture and river surfers at Brennan's Wave.

days.driving: Allow 15–25 minutes for local transit; conditions vary
days.note: Temperatures drop quickly after sunset; carry a light jacket even in summer.

days.title: Canyon Heights and Forest Silence

stops.name: Pattee Canyon Recreation Area
stops.detail: Navigate through towering ponderosa pines on an extensive network of trails suitable for hiking and mountain biking.

stops.name: Lolo National Forest
stops.detail: Drive toward the Bitterroot Valley to explore the foothills and historic mountain passes.

days.driving: Allow 45–75 minutes for forest roads; conditions vary
days.note: Check official Forest Service alerts for seasonal trail maintenance or fire closures.

days.title: Wildlife and Glacial History

stops.name: Lee Metcalf National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Drive south to observe migratory waterfowl and local bird species against the backdrop of the Bitterroot Mountains.

stops.name: Clark Fork River Overlooks
stops.detail: Stop at designated pullouts near Clinton to view the rugged canyons shaped by prehistoric glacial floods.

days.driving: Allow 60–90 minutes for regional loops; conditions vary
days.note: Maintain a safe distance from all wildlife and follow Leave No Trace principles.

intel.title: Trailhead Availability
intel.text: The 'M' Trail parking lot near the university fills early on weekends. Secondary parking is available in the downtown districts within walking distance of the river trails.

intel.title: Deep Canyon Coverage
intel.text: Reliable signals exist within the city limits and along the I-90 corridor. Service is often unavailable in the deeper sections of Pattee Canyon or Rock Creek.

intel.title: Corridor Services
intel.text: Fuel is plentiful in Missoula, Lolo, and Frenchtown. Services become sparse when traveling east toward the Blackfoot River or west over the mountain passes.

intel.title: High Season Windows
intel.text: July and August offer the most consistent weather for river activities. Late September brings color changes to the larches, though morning frosts are common.

intel.title: River Entry Points
intel.text: Designated fishing access sites (FAS) are the official points for launching tubes or boats. Private land boundaries are strictly enforced along the Blackfoot and Bitterroot rivers.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Missoula Montana Airport (MSO) and drive 12 minutes to downtown to check into your base and gather supplies.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for city and main road travel; high-clearance vehicles are recommended for forest service roads in the Lolo National Forest.
plan.goldenHour: Mount Sentinel provides a prime sunset viewpoint over the Garden City; check seasonal times as the sun hides behind the peaks early.
